label: August 1905
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1905 from our dossiers, placed on 1905 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 73 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1905. They come from the August 1905 table, which includes July events first reported in August, among them the lynching of Will Harris, taken from a train at Black Bayou, Mississippi, on July 28, and the West Side riots in New York. Several later checks added events. One found the lynching of a man named Bees near Rosetta, Mississippi, on August 31, missed at first because every report is dated September. Another linked the unnamed youth hanged at Cedar Bluff, Mississippi, to the Beck–Tolnay record of Cleveland McBee. A search of every August article for peonage added three cases, a check for attacks by one person added five, and leads in the dossiers added three more: a move-on order against Dr. Howard, a Black physician at Hattiesburg, the mob that formed there against Will Horn, and a police clubbing of a Black crowd in Harlem. We did not write dossiers for fourteen events that were plainly out of scope from the table alone: nine editorial or passing references to killings from earlier years, among them the 1904 burning of Cato and Reid at Statesboro, Georgia; three second records of episodes already held; a near-hanging at Erie, Pennsylvania, with no Black person involved; and an attempt by Black residents of a Texas town to lynch a Black suspect. Ten more belong to other months, among them the killing of eight jail prisoners at Watkinsville, Georgia, on June 29 and the lynching near Avery, Texas, on July 29. Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Fifteen of the 88 dossiers are set aside. Four describe events from other years: the 1904 threat to lynch Aaron Williams at Camden, South Carolina, a ball-game riot at Haughville, Indiana, that the page masthead dates to 1902, an undated rescue by Governor Vardaman, and an undated recollection from Peoria, Illinois. No report gives the victim’s race in three cases (Brooks King at Monroeville, Alabama; Horace Maples in Alabama; and a peonage arrest in Greenville County, South Carolina), and the dossier found no article behind a reported stoning of an excursion train at Barnwell, South Carolina. Two manhunts harmed no Black person, in two cases the attackers were Black or unnamed (a steamer near Baltimore and a camp meeting at Klondike, Georgia), two fights were two-sided (Raleigh, North Carolina, and an elevator in Minneapolis), and one lynching story is a secondhand anecdote with no date or place.

Police violence is kept generously: men shot while fleeing or resisting arrest are included, and only gunfights over a crime in progress are set aside from the totals. Peonage, force used to hold a Black worker to labor, is always included, even when the employer was Black, as at Baconton, Georgia. Where an inventory’s account differs from the press, the entry keeps the inventory link and states the difference: Beck–Tolnay lists the killing of Ike Kinney at Doella, Arkansas, as a lynching, while the papers describe a posse gunfight.

Attacks by one person: our definition covers violence by groups and by people acting with public authority, so an attack by a single private person is normally left out. A check of every August article for such attacks added a planter near Savannah who shot a Black farm hand and his son, a streetcar shooting in St. Louis, and a threat against a Black bellhop at a New Hampshire hotel, all kept and marked as one-person attacks.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched Black and white papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. Black-press clippings are shown as page images; white-press clippings are page images where we could place them on the scan, otherwise text.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
